Norovirus is NOT a nationally notifiable disease in the United States at the federal level; case counts are primarily captured through outbreak investigations (NORS) and sentinel surveillance (NoroSTAT/CaliciNet), not mandatory individual case reporting — aggregate and outbreak-level data will dominate.
NoroSTAT reports activity levels (not absolute case counts) — do not attempt numeric extraction from activity-level fields.
Seasonal peak for norovirus in the US is November–April; the target window (Dec 2024–Feb 2025) falls within peak season — expect elevated outbreak report volume.
Cruise ship outbreaks are reported to CDC Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) separately from land-based outbreaks — include VSP as a distinct source category.
Long-term care facility (LTCF) outbreaks are a dominant reporting context for norovirus in the US — prioritize LTCF-specific state and local health department reports.
Death data for norovirus is sparse and typically reported only in outbreak investigation reports for vulnerable populations — do not expect routine death surveillance data.
NORS data for the target window may not be publicly available in real time; check for data lag in NORS public access portal.
State health department reporting formats vary significantly — standardize subnational_location to state name and locality to city/county/facility as reported.
Evidence quotes must capture the exact numeric language used in the source (e.g., 'ill persons', 'confirmed cases', 'attack rate') to support downstream case classification mapping.

Do not conflate norovirus outbreak counts with total gastroenteritis burden estimates (e.g., CDC's 19–21 million annual cases estimate) — extract only empirically reported counts within the target time window.

count_semantics_notes: Norovirus case counts are frequently reported as 'ill persons' or 'affected individuals' rather than confirmed/probable/suspected — map to cases_unspecified unless laboratory confirmation is explicitly stated.
Laboratory-confirmed cases (RT-PCR or EIA) should be mapped to cases_confirmed.
Outbreak-level counts may aggregate across multiple case classification tiers — note aggregation in evidence_quote.
Attack rates are commonly reported for institutional outbreaks; derive absolute case counts only if denominator (population at risk) is explicitly stated.
Death counts for norovirus are rare and often reported only in vulnerable populations (elderly, immunocompromised); treat with high specificity — do not infer deaths from severity language alone.
Hospitalization counts may be reported separately from case counts; extract independently and note if derived from outbreak investigation vs. surveillance aggregate.
Seasonal surveillance data (e.g., NoroSTAT) reports activity levels (low/moderate/high/very high) rather than absolute case counts — do not convert activity levels to numeric case counts.
NORS data may report both primary and secondary cases; note distinction in evidence_quote.
Some state reports aggregate norovirus with 'acute gastroenteritis' — only extract if norovirus is explicitly named or laboratory-confirmed.
disambiguation_risks: 'Stomach flu' and 'stomach bug' are colloquial terms that may refer to norovirus or other enteric pathogens — require laboratory confirmation or explicit norovirus attribution before extraction.
Rotavirus, adenovirus, and sapovirus outbreaks may be reported alongside norovirus — extract only norovirus-specific counts.
Calicivirus may refer to animal calicivirus (e.g., feline calicivirus) — confirm human norovirus context.
'Viral gastroenteritis' without pathogen specification should be mapped to cases_unspecified and flagged for validation.
Norwalk virus is an older synonym — treat as norovirus if context confirms human enteric illness.
Norovirus GII.4 Sydney variant surges may be reported separately from aggregate norovirus counts — note genotype in evidence_quote if available.
Foodborne illness outbreak reports may list multiple pathogens; extract only norovirus-attributed counts.
Winter vomiting disease is a UK-centric term but may appear in US media coverage — confirm norovirus etiology before extraction.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Norovirus Gastroenteritis.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

count_semantics_notes: Norovirus case counts are frequently reported as 'ill persons' or 'affected individuals' rather than confirmed/probable/suspected — map to cases_unspecified unless laboratory confirmation is explicitly stated.
Laboratory-confirmed cases (RT-PCR or EIA) should be mapped to cases_confirmed.
Outbreak-level counts may aggregate across multiple case classification tiers — note aggregation in evidence_quote.
Attack rates are commonly reported for institutional outbreaks; derive absolute case counts only if denominator (population at risk) is explicitly stated.
Death counts for norovirus are rare and often reported only in vulnerable populations (elderly, immunocompromised); treat with high specificity — do not infer deaths from severity language alone.
Hospitalization counts may be reported separately from case counts; extract independently and note if derived from outbreak investigation vs. surveillance aggregate.
Seasonal surveillance data (e.g., NoroSTAT) reports activity levels (low/moderate/high/very high) rather than absolute case counts — do not convert activity levels to numeric case counts.
NORS data may report both primary and secondary cases; note distinction in evidence_quote.
Some state reports aggregate norovirus with 'acute gastroenteritis' — only extract if norovirus is explicitly named or laboratory-confirmed.
disambiguation_risks: 'Stomach flu' and 'stomach bug' are colloquial terms that may refer to norovirus or other enteric pathogens — require laboratory confirmation or explicit norovirus attribution before extraction.
Rotavirus, adenovirus, and sapovirus outbreaks may be reported alongside norovirus — extract only norovirus-specific counts.
Calicivirus may refer to animal calicivirus (e.g., feline calicivirus) — confirm human norovirus context.
'Viral gastroenteritis' without pathogen specification should be mapped to cases_unspecified and flagged for validation.
Norwalk virus is an older synonym — treat as norovirus if context confirms human enteric illness.
Norovirus GII.4 Sydney variant surges may be reported separately from aggregate norovirus counts — note genotype in evidence_quote if available.
Foodborne illness outbreak reports may list multiple pathogens; extract only norovirus-attributed counts.
Winter vomiting disease is a UK-centric term but may appear in US media coverage — confirm norovirus etiology before extraction.

Norovirus is NOT a nationally notifiable disease in the United States at the federal level; case counts are primarily captured through outbreak investigations (NORS) and sentinel surveillance (NoroSTAT/CaliciNet), not mandatory individual case reporting — aggregate and outbreak-level data will dominate.
NoroSTAT reports activity levels (not absolute case counts) — do not attempt numeric extraction from activity-level fields.
Seasonal peak for norovirus in the US is November–April; the target window (Dec 2024–Feb 2025) falls within peak season — expect elevated outbreak report volume.
Cruise ship outbreaks are reported to CDC Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) separately from land-based outbreaks — include VSP as a distinct source category.
Long-term care facility (LTCF) outbreaks are a dominant reporting context for norovirus in the US — prioritize LTCF-specific state and local health department reports.
Death data for norovirus is sparse and typically reported only in outbreak investigation reports for vulnerable populations — do not expect routine death surveillance data.
NORS data for the target window may not be publicly available in real time; check for data lag in NORS public access portal.
State health department reporting formats vary significantly — standardize subnational_location to state name and locality to city/county/facility as reported.
Evidence quotes must capture the exact numeric language used in the source (e.g., 'ill persons', 'confirmed cases', 'attack rate') to support downstream case classification mapping.

Do not conflate norovirus outbreak counts with total gastroenteritis burden estimates (e.g., CDC's 19–21 million annual cases estimate) — extract only empirically reported counts within the target time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) data or summaries covering norovirus outbreaks reported in the United States from 2024-12-01 to 2025-02-28.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NORS is the authoritative US database for foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks including norovirus, with case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and setting data.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, New York DOH, Texas DSHS) often publish outbreak-specific reports with subnational location, case counts, and dates that supplement national surveillance.

count_semantics_notes: Norovirus case counts are frequently reported as 'ill persons' or 'affected individuals' rather than confirmed/probable/suspected — map to cases_unspecified unless laboratory confirmation is explicitly stated.
Laboratory-confirmed cases (RT-PCR or EIA) should be mapped to cases_confirmed.
Outbreak-level counts may aggregate across multiple case classification tiers — note aggregation in evidence_quote.
Attack rates are commonly reported for institutional outbreaks; derive absolute case counts only if denominator (population at risk) is explicitly stated.
Death counts for norovirus are rare and often reported only in vulnerable populations (elderly, immunocompromised); treat with high specificity — do not infer deaths from severity language alone.
Hospitalization counts may be reported separately from case counts; extract independently and note if derived from outbreak investigation vs. surveillance aggregate.
Seasonal surveillance data (e.g., NoroSTAT) reports activity levels (low/moderate/high/very high) rather than absolute case counts — do not convert activity levels to numeric case counts.
NORS data may report both primary and secondary cases; note distinction in evidence_quote.
Some state reports aggregate norovirus with 'acute gastroenteritis' — only extract if norovirus is explicitly named or laboratory-confirmed.
disambiguation_risks: 'Stomach flu' and 'stomach bug' are colloquial terms that may refer to norovirus or other enteric pathogens — require laboratory confirmation or explicit norovirus attribution before extraction.
Rotavirus, adenovirus, and sapovirus outbreaks may be reported alongside norovirus — extract only norovirus-specific counts.
Calicivirus may refer to animal calicivirus (e.g., feline calicivirus) — confirm human norovirus context.
'Viral gastroenteritis' without pathogen specification should be mapped to cases_unspecified and flagged for validation.
Norwalk virus is an older synonym — treat as norovirus if context confirms human enteric illness.
Norovirus GII.4 Sydney variant surges may be reported separately from aggregate norovirus counts — note genotype in evidence_quote if available.
Foodborne illness outbreak reports may list multiple pathogens; extract only norovirus-attributed counts.
Winter vomiting disease is a UK-centric term but may appear in US media coverage — confirm norovirus etiology before extraction.

Norovirus is NOT a nationally notifiable disease in the United States at the federal level; case counts are primarily captured through outbreak investigations (NORS) and sentinel surveillance (NoroSTAT/CaliciNet), not mandatory individual case reporting — aggregate and outbreak-level data will dominate.
NoroSTAT reports activity levels (not absolute case counts) — do not attempt numeric extraction from activity-level fields.

count_semantics_notes: Norovirus case counts are frequently reported as 'ill persons' or 'affected individuals' rather than confirmed/probable/suspected — map to cases_unspecified unless laboratory confirmation is explicitly stated.
Laboratory-confirmed cases (RT-PCR or EIA) should be mapped to cases_confirmed.
Outbreak-level counts may aggregate across multiple case classification tiers — note aggregation in evidence_quote.
Attack rates are commonly reported for institutional outbreaks; derive absolute case counts only if denominator (population at risk) is explicitly stated.
Death counts for norovirus are rare and often reported only in vulnerable populations (elderly, immunocompromised); treat with high specificity — do not infer deaths from severity language alone.
Hospitalization counts may be reported separately from case counts; extract independently and note if derived from outbreak investigation vs. surveillance aggregate.
Seasonal surveillance data (e.g., NoroSTAT) reports activity levels (low/moderate/high/very high) rather than absolute case counts — do not convert activity levels to numeric case counts.
NORS data may report both primary and secondary cases; note distinction in evidence_quote.
Some state reports aggregate norovirus with 'acute gastroenteritis' — only extract if norovirus is explicitly named or laboratory-confirmed.
disambiguation_risks: 'Stomach flu' and 'stomach bug' are colloquial terms that may refer to norovirus or other enteric pathogens — require laboratory confirmation or explicit norovirus attribution before extraction.
Rotavirus, adenovirus, and sapovirus outbreaks may be reported alongside norovirus — extract only norovirus-specific counts.
Calicivirus may refer to animal calicivirus (e.g., feline calicivirus) — confirm human norovirus context.
'Viral gastroenteritis' without pathogen specification should be mapped to cases_unspecified and flagged for validation.
Norwalk virus is an older synonym — treat as norovirus if context confirms human enteric illness.
Norovirus GII.4 Sydney variant surges may be reported separately from aggregate norovirus counts — note genotype in evidence_quote if available.
Foodborne illness outbreak reports may list multiple pathogens; extract only norovirus-attributed counts.
Winter vomiting disease is a UK-centric term but may appear in US media coverage — confirm norovirus etiology before extraction.

Seasonal peak for norovirus in the US is November–April; the target window (Dec 2024–Feb 2025) falls within peak season — expect elevated outbreak report volume.
Cruise ship outbreaks are reported to CDC Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) separately from land-based outbreaks — include VSP as a distinct source category.
Long-term care facility (LTCF) outbreaks are a dominant reporting context for norovirus in the US — prioritize LTCF-specific state and local health department reports.
Death data for norovirus is sparse and typically reported only in outbreak investigation reports for vulnerable populations — do not expect routine death surveillance data.
NORS data for the target window may not be publicly available in real time; check for data lag in NORS public access portal.
State health department reporting formats vary significantly — standardize subnational_location to state name and locality to city/county/facility as reported.

disease_intelligence.suggested_time_granularity: ["weekly (preferred for surveillance data)", "monthly (for aggregate reports)", "outbreak-specific date range (onset to resolution)", "date of report publication"]
count_semantics_notes: Norovirus case counts are frequently reported as 'ill persons' or 'affected individuals' rather than confirmed/probable/suspected — map to cases_unspecified unless laboratory confirmation is explicitly stated.
Laboratory-confirmed cases (RT-PCR or EIA) should be mapped to cases_confirmed.
Outbreak-level counts may aggregate across multiple case classification tiers — note aggregation in evidence_quote.
Attack rates are commonly reported for institutional outbreaks; derive absolute case counts only if denominator (population at risk) is explicitly stated.
Death counts for norovirus are rare and often reported only in vulnerable populations (elderly, immunocompromised); treat with high specificity — do not infer deaths from severity language alone.
Hospitalization counts may be reported separately from case counts; extract independently and note if derived from outbreak investigation vs. surveillance aggregate.
Seasonal surveillance data (e.g., NoroSTAT) reports activity levels (low/moderate/high/very high) rather than absolute case counts — do not convert activity levels to numeric case counts.
NORS data may report both primary and secondary cases; note distinction in evidence_quote.
Some state reports aggregate norovirus with 'acute gastroenteritis' — only extract if norovirus is explicitly named or laboratory-confirmed.
disambiguation_risks: 'Stomach flu' and 'stomach bug' are colloquial terms that may refer to norovirus or other enteric pathogens — require laboratory confirmation or explicit norovirus attribution before extraction.
Rotavirus, adenovirus, and sapovirus outbreaks may be reported alongside norovirus — extract only norovirus-specific counts.
Calicivirus may refer to animal calicivirus (e.g., feline calicivirus) — confirm human norovirus context.
'Viral gastroenteritis' without pathogen specification should be mapped to cases_unspecified and flagged for validation.

count_semantics_notes: Norovirus case counts are frequently reported as 'ill persons' or 'affected individuals' rather than confirmed/probable/suspected — map to cases_unspecified unless laboratory confirmation is explicitly stated.
Laboratory-confirmed cases (RT-PCR or EIA) should be mapped to cases_confirmed.
Outbreak-level counts may aggregate across multiple case classification tiers — note aggregation in evidence_quote.
Attack rates are commonly reported for institutional outbreaks; derive absolute case counts only if denominator (population at risk) is explicitly stated.
Death counts for norovirus are rare and often reported only in vulnerable populations (elderly, immunocompromised); treat with high specificity — do not infer deaths from severity language alone.
Hospitalization counts may be reported separately from case counts; extract independently and note if derived from outbreak investigation vs. surveillance aggregate.
Seasonal surveillance data (e.g., NoroSTAT) reports activity levels (low/moderate/high/very high) rather than absolute case counts — do not convert activity levels to numeric case counts.
NORS data may report both primary and secondary cases; note distinction in evidence_quote.
Some state reports aggregate norovirus with 'acute gastroenteritis' — only extract if norovirus is explicitly named or laboratory-confirmed.
disambiguation_risks: 'Stomach flu' and 'stomach bug' are colloquial terms that may refer to norovirus or other enteric pathogens — require laboratory confirmation or explicit norovirus attribution before extraction.
Rotavirus, adenovirus, and sapovirus outbreaks may be reported alongside norovirus — extract only norovirus-specific counts.
Calicivirus may refer to animal calicivirus (e.g., feline calicivirus) — confirm human norovirus context.
'Viral gastroenteritis' without pathogen specification should be mapped to cases_unspecified and flagged for validation.
Norwalk virus is an older synonym — treat as norovirus if context confirms human enteric illness.
Norovirus GII.4 Sydney variant surges may be reported separately from aggregate norovirus counts — note genotype in evidence_quote if available.
Foodborne illness outbreak reports may list multiple pathogens; extract only norovirus-attributed counts.
Winter vomiting disease is a UK-centric term but may appear in US media coverage — confirm norovirus etiology before extraction.

Norovirus is NOT a nationally notifiable disease in the United States at the federal level; case counts are primarily captured through outbreak investigations (NORS) and sentinel surveillance (NoroSTAT/CaliciNet), not mandatory individual case reporting — aggregate and outbreak-level data will dominate.
NoroSTAT reports activity levels (not absolute case counts) — do not attempt numeric extraction from activity-level fields.
Seasonal peak for norovirus in the US is November–April; the target window (Dec 2024–Feb 2025) falls within peak season — expect elevated outbreak report volume.
Cruise ship outbreaks are reported to CDC Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) separately from land-based outbreaks — include VSP as a distinct source category.
Long-term care facility (LTCF) outbreaks are a dominant reporting context for norovirus in the US — prioritize LTCF-specific state and local health department reports.
Death data for norovirus is sparse and typically reported only in outbreak investigation reports for vulnerable populations — do not expect routine death surveillance data.
NORS data for the target window may not be publicly available in real time; check for data lag in NORS public access portal.
State health department reporting formats vary significantly — standardize subnational_location to state name and locality to city/county/facility as reported.
Evidence quotes must capture the exact numeric language used in the source (e.g., 'ill persons', 'confirmed cases', 'attack rate') to support downstream case classification mapping.

Do not conflate norovirus outbreak counts with total gastroenteritis burden estimates (e.g., CDC's 19–21 million annual cases estimate) — extract only empirically reported counts within the target time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC norovirus surveillance pages (NoroSTAT, CaliciNet) reporting outbreak counts, case totals, and activity levels for the United States during December 2024 through February 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC is the primary national authority for norovirus surveillance in the US. NoroSTAT tracks outbreak counts by setting and CaliciNet tracks genotype-level data; both are primary extractable collection sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) data or summaries covering norovirus outbreaks reported in the United States from 2024-12-01 to 2025-02-28.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NORS is the authoritative US database for foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks including norovirus, with case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and setting data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state and local health department outbreak reports, press releases, or situation reports for norovirus in the United States during the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, New York DOH, Texas DSHS) often publish outbreak-specific reports with subnational location, case counts, and dates that supplement national surveillance.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR) articles or notices reporting norovirus outbreaks or case counts in the United States for the target period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR frequently publishes norovirus outbreak investigations with confirmed case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and evidence quotes suitable for extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO or PAHO situation reports or disease outbreak news referencing norovirus activity in the United States during 2024-12-01 to 2025-02-28.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports provide independent aggregate summaries that can validate CDC-reported figures without being the primary collection source.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured databases such as HealthMap, ProMED, or GOARN alerts referencing norovirus outbreaks in the United States during the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured alert databases aggregate outbreak signals from multiple sources and can serve as independent validation of case counts and outbreak events.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definition pages, norovirus background pages, and surveillance methodology documents to support correct interpretation of case classification fields.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC's case definitions for confirmed, probable, and suspected norovirus is essential for correctly populating cases_confirmed, cases_probable, and cases_suspected fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature published in 2024-2025 describing norovirus epidemiology, outbreak patterns, or surveillance methodology in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Recent literature provides context for interpreting surveillance data, genotype distributions, and outbreak settings relevant to the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news reports covering specific norovirus outbreaks in the United States from December 2024 through February 2025, particularly those citing official case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may surface outbreak events (e.g., cruise ship, school, long-term care facility) with case counts and dates before official reports are published, serving as leads for official source follow-up.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (e.g., cumulative vs. newly reported, suspected vs. confirmed), where validation and collection roles may overlap, or where subnational attribution is unclear.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Norovirus surveillance data often mixes outbreak-level and aggregate counts; human review is needed to resolve ambiguous count types and prevent validation leakage.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC (NoroSTAT, CaliciNet, NORS, MMWR) and state/local health departments are the primary authoritative sources for norovirus case counts, outbreak reports, deaths, and hospitalizations in the United States. These sources are most likely to contain extractable records matching the target fields and time window.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and PAHO epidemiological alerts may reference US norovirus activity and provide independent aggregate figures for validation against CDC-sourced collection records.

ProMED, HealthMap, and similar structured outbreak alert databases aggregate norovirus outbreak signals from official and media sources, enabling independent cross-validation of outbreak events and case counts.

Peer-reviewed outbreak investigations and surveillance studies published in 2024-2025 may contain case series data, outbreak descriptions, and case definitions relevant to the target window and useful for contextualizing extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (AP, Reuters, local news) and situation reports may cover specific norovirus outbreaks (cruise ships, schools, long-term care facilities) with case counts and dates, providing leads for official source follow-up and supplementary collection support.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Norovirus surveillance data often mixes outbreak-level and aggregate counts; human review is needed to resolve ambiguous count types and prevent validation leakage.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC (NoroSTAT, CaliciNet, NORS, MMWR) and state/local health departments are the primary authoritative sources for norovirus case counts, outbreak reports, deaths, and hospitalizations in the United States. These sources are most likely to contain extractable records matching the target fields and time window.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and PAHO epidemiological alerts may reference US norovirus activity and provide independent aggregate figures for validation against CDC-sourced collection records.

ProMED, HealthMap, and similar structured outbreak alert databases aggregate norovirus outbreak signals from official and media sources, enabling independent cross-validation of outbreak events and case counts.

Peer-reviewed outbreak investigations and surveillance studies published in 2024-2025 may contain case series data, outbreak descriptions, and case definitions relevant to the target window and useful for contextualizing extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (AP, Reuters, local news) and situation reports may cover specific norovirus outbreaks (cruise ships, schools, long-term care facilities) with case counts and dates, providing leads for official source follow-up and supplementary collection support.

query_batch.query: CDC NoroSTAT norovirus surveillance 2024 2025 season United States cases outbreaks
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC NoroSTAT is the primary US national norovirus surveillance system. This query directly targets the CDC's seasonal surveillance summary, which is the highest-priority authoritative source for national-level case and outbreak counts. Natural-language phrasing without exact-phrase quoting improves recall over the upstream query formulation.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC NoroSTAT weekly surveillance summary or season overview page with outbreak counts, case totals, and trend data for the 2024-2025 norovirus season
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; authored by CDC Division of Viral Diseases; references NORS data

query_batch.query: CDC NORS norovirus outbreak reports United States December 2024 January February 2025 cases hospitalizations deaths
query_batch.query_rationale: NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) is the CDC's structured database for foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks including norovirus. It provides outbreak-level records with subnational location, setting, case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths — directly mapping to the target fields. Querying NORS for the specific months in the task window maximizes coverage of the locality and subnational_location fields.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC NORS dashboard or data summary page listing individual norovirus outbreak records with setting, state, case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths for the target date range
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov/nors domain; structured outbreak-level records with state and setting fields

query_batch.query: norovirus outbreak United States winter 2024 2025 cases deaths state health department report
query_batch.query_rationale: Because norovirus is not nationally notifiable, subnational outbreak data is primarily reported at the state and local level. This broad web search targets state health department reports and press releases that would populate the subnational_location and locality fields. The query avoids exact-phrase quoting to maximize recall across diverse state agency naming conventions.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: State or local health department press releases, epidemiology bulletins, or outbreak investigation reports with specific case counts, dates, and geographic locations within the US
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: State .gov domains (e.g., health.state.xx.us); official press release or epi bulletin format; named public health official quoted

count_semantics_notes: Norovirus case counts are frequently reported as 'ill persons' or 'affected individuals' rather than confirmed/probable/suspected — map to cases_unspecified unless laboratory confirmation is explicitly stated.
Laboratory-confirmed cases (RT-PCR or EIA) should be mapped to cases_confirmed.
Outbreak-level counts may aggregate across multiple case classification tiers — note aggregation in evidence_quote.
Attack rates are commonly reported for institutional outbreaks; derive absolute case counts only if denominator (population at risk) is explicitly stated.
Death counts for norovirus are rare and often reported only in vulnerable populations (elderly, immunocompromised); treat with high specificity — do not infer deaths from severity language alone.
Hospitalization counts may be reported separately from case counts; extract independently and note if derived from outbreak investigation vs. surveillance aggregate.
Seasonal surveillance data (e.g., NoroSTAT) reports activity levels (low/moderate/high/very high) rather than absolute case counts — do not convert activity levels to numeric case counts.
NORS data may report both primary and secondary cases; note distinction in evidence_quote.
Some state reports aggregate norovirus with 'acute gastroenteritis' — only extract if norovirus is explicitly named or laboratory-confirmed.
disambiguation_risks: 'Stomach flu' and 'stomach bug' are colloquial terms that may refer to norovirus or other enteric pathogens — require laboratory confirmation or explicit norovirus attribution before extraction.
Rotavirus, adenovirus, and sapovirus outbreaks may be reported alongside norovirus — extract only norovirus-specific counts.
Calicivirus may refer to animal calicivirus (e.g., feline calicivirus) — confirm human norovirus context.
'Viral gastroenteritis' without pathogen specification should be mapped to cases_unspecified and flagged for validation.
Norwalk virus is an older synonym — treat as norovirus if context confirms human enteric illness.
Norovirus GII.4 Sydney variant surges may be reported separately from aggregate norovirus counts — note genotype in evidence_quote if available.
Foodborne illness outbreak reports may list multiple pathogens; extract only norovirus-attributed counts.
Winter vomiting disease is a UK-centric term but may appear in US media coverage — confirm norovirus etiology before extraction.

Norovirus is NOT a nationally notifiable disease in the United States at the federal level; case counts are primarily captured through outbreak investigations (NORS) and sentinel surveillance (NoroSTAT/CaliciNet), not mandatory individual case reporting — aggregate and outbreak-level data will dominate.
NoroSTAT reports activity levels (not absolute case counts) — do not attempt numeric extraction from activity-level fields.
Seasonal peak for norovirus in the US is November–April; the target window (Dec 2024–Feb 2025) falls within peak season — expect elevated outbreak report volume.
Cruise ship outbreaks are reported to CDC Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) separately from land-based outbreaks — include VSP as a distinct source category.
Long-term care facility (LTCF) outbreaks are a dominant reporting context for norovirus in the US — prioritize LTCF-specific state and local health department reports.
Death data for norovirus is sparse and typically reported only in outbreak investigation reports for vulnerable populations — do not expect routine death surveillance data.
NORS data for the target window may not be publicly available in real time; check for data lag in NORS public access portal.
State health department reporting formats vary significantly — standardize subnational_location to state name and locality to city/county/facility as reported.
Evidence quotes must capture the exact numeric language used in the source (e.g., 'ill persons', 'confirmed cases', 'attack rate') to support downstream case classification mapping.

Do not conflate norovirus outbreak counts with total gastroenteritis burden estimates (e.g., CDC's 19–21 million annual cases estimate) — extract only empirically reported counts within the target time window.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Norovirus Gastroenteritis.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.

query_batch.query_rationale: CDC NoroSTAT is the primary US national norovirus surveillance system. query_batch.query: CDC NORS norovirus outbreak reports United States December 2024 January February 2025 cases hospitalizations deaths
query_batch.query_rationale: NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) is the CDC's structured database for foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks including norovirus. It provides outbreak-level records with subnational location, setting, case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths — directly mapping to the target fields. Querying NORS for the specific months in the task window maximizes coverage of the locality and subnational_location fields.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC NORS dashboard or data summary page listing individual norovirus outbreak records with setting, state, case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths for the target date range
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov/nors domain; structured outbreak-level records with state and setting fields

query_batch.query: norovirus outbreak United States winter 2024 2025 cases deaths state health department report

The query avoids exact-phrase quoting to maximize recall across diverse state agency naming conventions.

count_semantics_notes: Norovirus case counts are frequently reported as 'ill persons' or 'affected individuals' rather than confirmed/probable/suspected — map to cases_unspecified unless laboratory confirmation is explicitly stated.
Laboratory-confirmed cases (RT-PCR or EIA) should be mapped to cases_confirmed.
Outbreak-level counts may aggregate across multiple case classification tiers — note aggregation in evidence_quote.
Attack rates are commonly reported for institutional outbreaks; derive absolute case counts only if denominator (population at risk) is explicitly stated.
Death counts for norovirus are rare and often reported only in vulnerable populations (elderly, immunocompromised); treat with high specificity — do not infer deaths from severity language alone.
Hospitalization counts may be reported separately from case counts; extract independently and note if derived from outbreak investigation vs. surveillance aggregate.
Seasonal surveillance data (e.g., NoroSTAT) reports activity levels (low/moderate/high/very high) rather than absolute case counts — do not convert activity levels to numeric case counts.
NORS data may report both primary and secondary cases; note distinction in evidence_quote.
Some state reports aggregate norovirus with 'acute gastroenteritis' — only extract if norovirus is explicitly named or laboratory-confirmed.
disambiguation_risks: 'Stomach flu' and 'stomach bug' are colloquial terms that may refer to norovirus or other enteric pathogens — require laboratory confirmation or explicit norovirus attribution before extraction.
Rotavirus, adenovirus, and sapovirus outbreaks may be reported alongside norovirus — extract only norovirus-specific counts.
Calicivirus may refer to animal calicivirus (e.g., feline calicivirus) — confirm human norovirus context.
'Viral gastroenteritis' without pathogen specification should be mapped to cases_unspecified and flagged for validation.
Norwalk virus is an older synonym — treat as norovirus if context confirms human enteric illness.
Norovirus GII.4 Sydney variant surges may be reported separately from aggregate norovirus counts — note genotype in evidence_quote if available.
Foodborne illness outbreak reports may list multiple pathogens; extract only norovirus-attributed counts.
Winter vomiting disease is a UK-centric term but may appear in US media coverage — confirm norovirus etiology before extraction.

Norovirus is NOT a nationally notifiable disease in the United States at the federal level; case counts are primarily captured through outbreak investigations (NORS) and sentinel surveillance (NoroSTAT/CaliciNet), not mandatory individual case reporting — aggregate and outbreak-level data will dominate.
NoroSTAT reports activity levels (not absolute case counts) — do not attempt numeric extraction from activity-level fields.
Seasonal peak for norovirus in the US is November–April; the target window (Dec 2024–Feb 2025) falls within peak season — expect elevated outbreak report volume.
Cruise ship outbreaks are reported to CDC Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) separately from land-based outbreaks — include VSP as a distinct source category.
Long-term care facility (LTCF) outbreaks are a dominant reporting context for norovirus in the US — prioritize LTCF-specific state and local health department reports.
Death data for norovirus is sparse and typically reported only in outbreak investigation reports for vulnerable populations — do not expect routine death surveillance data.
NORS data for the target window may not be publicly available in real time; check for data lag in NORS public access portal.
State health department reporting formats vary significantly — standardize subnational_location to state name and locality to city/county/facility as reported.
Evidence quotes must capture the exact numeric language used in the source (e.g., 'ill persons', 'confirmed cases', 'attack rate') to support downstream case classification mapping.

Do not conflate norovirus outbreak counts with total gastroenteritis burden estimates (e.g., CDC's 19–21 million annual cases estimate) — extract only empirically reported counts within the target time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC norovirus surveillance pages (NoroSTAT, CaliciNet) reporting outbreak counts, case totals, and activity levels for the United States during December 2024 through February 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC is the primary national authority for norovirus surveillance in the US. NoroSTAT tracks outbreak counts by setting and CaliciNet tracks genotype-level data; both are primary extractable collection sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) data or summaries covering norovirus outbreaks reported in the United States from 2024-12-01 to 2025-02-28.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NORS is the authoritative US database for foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks including norovirus, with case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and setting data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state and local health department outbreak reports, press releases, or situation reports for norovirus in the United States during the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, New York DOH, Texas DSHS) often publish outbreak-specific reports with subnational location, case counts, and dates that supplement national surveillance.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR) articles or notices reporting norovirus outbreaks or case counts in the United States for the target period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR frequently publishes norovirus outbreak investigations with confirmed case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and evidence quotes suitable for extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO or PAHO situation reports or disease outbreak news referencing norovirus activity in the United States during 2024-12-01 to 2025-02-28.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports provide independent aggregate summaries that can validate CDC-reported figures without being the primary collection source.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured databases such as HealthMap, ProMED, or GOARN alerts referencing norovirus outbreaks in the United States during the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured alert databases aggregate outbreak signals from multiple sources and can serve as independent validation of case counts and outbreak events.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definition pages, norovirus background pages, and surveillance methodology documents to support correct interpretation of case classification fields.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC's case definitions for confirmed, probable, and suspected norovirus is essential for correctly populating cases_confirmed, cases_probable, and cases_suspected fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature published in 2024-2025 describing norovirus epidemiology, outbreak patterns, or surveillance methodology in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Recent literature provides context for interpreting surveillance data, genotype distributions, and outbreak settings relevant to the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news reports covering specific norovirus outbreaks in the United States from December 2024 through February 2025, particularly those citing official case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may surface outbreak events (e.g., cruise ship, school, long-term care facility) with case counts and dates before official reports are published, serving as leads for official source follow-up.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (e.g., cumulative vs. newly reported, suspected vs. confirmed), where validation and collection roles may overlap, or where subnational attribution is unclear.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Norovirus surveillance data often mixes outbreak-level and aggregate counts; human review is needed to resolve ambiguous count types and prevent validation leakage.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC (NoroSTAT, CaliciNet, NORS, MMWR) and state/local health departments are the primary authoritative sources for norovirus case counts, outbreak reports, deaths, and hospitalizations in the United States. These sources are most likely to contain extractable records matching the target fields and time window.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and PAHO epidemiological alerts may reference US norovirus activity and provide independent aggregate figures for validation against CDC-sourced collection records.

ProMED, HealthMap, and similar structured outbreak alert databases aggregate norovirus outbreak signals from official and media sources, enabling independent cross-validation of outbreak events and case counts.

Peer-reviewed outbreak investigations and surveillance studies published in 2024-2025 may contain case series data, outbreak descriptions, and case definitions relevant to the target window and useful for contextualizing extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (AP, Reuters, local news) and situation reports may cover specific norovirus outbreaks (cruise ships, schools, long-term care facilities) with case counts and dates, providing leads for official source follow-up and supplementary collection support.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC norovirus surveillance pages (NoroSTAT, CaliciNet) reporting outbreak counts, case totals, and activity levels for the United States during December 2024 through February 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC is the primary national authority for norovirus surveillance in the US. NoroSTAT tracks outbreak counts by setting and CaliciNet tracks genotype-level data; both are primary extractable collection sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) data or summaries covering norovirus outbreaks reported in the United States from 2024-12-01 to 2025-02-28.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NORS is the authoritative US database for foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks including norovirus, with case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and setting data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state and local health department outbreak reports, press releases, or situation reports for norovirus in the United States during the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, New York DOH, Texas DSHS) often publish outbreak-specific reports with subnational location, case counts, and dates that supplement national surveillance.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR) articles or notices reporting norovirus outbreaks or case counts in the United States for the target period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR frequently publishes norovirus outbreak investigations with confirmed case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and evidence quotes suitable for extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO or PAHO situation reports or disease outbreak news referencing norovirus activity in the United States during 2024-12-01 to 2025-02-28.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports provide independent aggregate summaries that can validate CDC-reported figures without being the primary collection source.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured databases such as HealthMap, ProMED, or GOARN alerts referencing norovirus outbreaks in the United States during the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured alert databases aggregate outbreak signals from multiple sources and can serve as independent validation of case counts and outbreak events.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definition pages, norovirus background pages, and surveillance methodology documents to support correct interpretation of case classification fields.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC's case definitions for confirmed, probable, and suspected norovirus is essential for correctly populating cases_confirmed, cases_probable, and cases_suspected fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature published in 2024-2025 describing norovirus epidemiology, outbreak patterns, or surveillance methodology in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Recent literature provides context for interpreting surveillance data, genotype distributions, and outbreak settings relevant to the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news reports covering specific norovirus outbreaks in the United States from December 2024 through February 2025, particularly those citing official case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may surface outbreak events (e.g., cruise ship, school, long-term care facility) with case counts and dates before official reports are published, serving as leads for official source follow-up.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (e.g., cumulative vs. newly reported, suspected vs. confirmed), where validation and collection roles may overlap, or where subnational attribution is unclear.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Norovirus surveillance data often mixes outbreak-level and aggregate counts; human review is needed to resolve ambiguous count types and prevent validation leakage.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC (NoroSTAT, CaliciNet, NORS, MMWR) and state/local health departments are the primary authoritative sources for norovirus case counts, outbreak reports, deaths, and hospitalizations in the United States. These sources are most likely to contain extractable records matching the target fields and time window.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and PAHO epidemiological alerts may reference US norovirus activity and provide independent aggregate figures for validation against CDC-sourced collection records.

ProMED, HealthMap, and similar structured outbreak alert databases aggregate norovirus outbreak signals from official and media sources, enabling independent cross-validation of outbreak events and case counts.

Peer-reviewed outbreak investigations and surveillance studies published in 2024-2025 may contain case series data, outbreak descriptions, and case definitions relevant to the target window and useful for contextualizing extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (AP, Reuters, local news) and situation reports may cover specific norovirus outbreaks (cruise ships, schools, long-term care facilities) with case counts and dates, providing leads for official source follow-up and supplementary collection support.

count_semantics_notes: Norovirus case counts are frequently reported as 'ill persons' or 'affected individuals' rather than confirmed/probable/suspected — map to cases_unspecified unless laboratory confirmation is explicitly stated.
Laboratory-confirmed cases (RT-PCR or EIA) should be mapped to cases_confirmed.
Outbreak-level counts may aggregate across multiple case classification tiers — note aggregation in evidence_quote.
Attack rates are commonly reported for institutional outbreaks; derive absolute case counts only if denominator (population at risk) is explicitly stated.
Death counts for norovirus are rare and often reported only in vulnerable populations (elderly, immunocompromised); treat with high specificity — do not infer deaths from severity language alone.
Hospitalization counts may be reported separately from case counts; extract independently and note if derived from outbreak investigation vs. surveillance aggregate.
Seasonal surveillance data (e.g., NoroSTAT) reports activity levels (low/moderate/high/very high) rather than absolute case counts — do not convert activity levels to numeric case counts.
NORS data may report both primary and secondary cases; note distinction in evidence_quote.
Some state reports aggregate norovirus with 'acute gastroenteritis' — only extract if norovirus is explicitly named or laboratory-confirmed.
disambiguation_risks: 'Stomach flu' and 'stomach bug' are colloquial terms that may refer to norovirus or other enteric pathogens — require laboratory confirmation or explicit norovirus attribution before extraction.
Rotavirus, adenovirus, and sapovirus outbreaks may be reported alongside norovirus — extract only norovirus-specific counts.
Calicivirus may refer to animal calicivirus (e.g., feline calicivirus) — confirm human norovirus context.
'Viral gastroenteritis' without pathogen specification should be mapped to cases_unspecified and flagged for validation.
Norwalk virus is an older synonym — treat as norovirus if context confirms human enteric illness.
Norovirus GII.4 Sydney variant surges may be reported separately from aggregate norovirus counts — note genotype in evidence_quote if available.
Foodborne illness outbreak reports may list multiple pathogens; extract only norovirus-attributed counts.
Winter vomiting disease is a UK-centric term but may appear in US media coverage — confirm norovirus etiology before extraction.

Norovirus is NOT a nationally notifiable disease in the United States at the federal level; case counts are primarily captured through outbreak investigations (NORS) and sentinel surveillance (NoroSTAT/CaliciNet), not mandatory individual case reporting — aggregate and outbreak-level data will dominate.
NoroSTAT reports activity levels (not absolute case counts) — do not attempt numeric extraction from activity-level fields.
Seasonal peak for norovirus in the US is November–April; the target window (Dec 2024–Feb 2025) falls within peak season — expect elevated outbreak report volume.
Cruise ship outbreaks are reported to CDC Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) separately from land-based outbreaks — include VSP as a distinct source category.
Long-term care facility (LTCF) outbreaks are a dominant reporting context for norovirus in the US — prioritize LTCF-specific state and local health department reports.
Death data for norovirus is sparse and typically reported only in outbreak investigation reports for vulnerable populations — do not expect routine death surveillance data.
NORS data for the target window may not be publicly available in real time; check for data lag in NORS public access portal.
State health department reporting formats vary significantly — standardize subnational_location to state name and locality to city/county/facility as reported.
Evidence quotes must capture the exact numeric language used in the source (e.g., 'ill persons', 'confirmed cases', 'attack rate') to support downstream case classification mapping.

Do not conflate norovirus outbreak counts with total gastroenteritis burden estimates (e.g., CDC's 19–21 million annual cases estimate) — extract only empirically reported counts within the target time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC norovirus surveillance pages (NoroSTAT, CaliciNet) reporting outbreak counts, case totals, and activity levels for the United States during December 2024 through February 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC is the primary national authority for norovirus surveillance in the US. NoroSTAT tracks outbreak counts by setting and CaliciNet tracks genotype-level data; both are primary extractable collection sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) data or summaries covering norovirus outbreaks reported in the United States from 2024-12-01 to 2025-02-28.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NORS is the authoritative US database for foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks including norovirus, with case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and setting data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state and local health department outbreak reports, press releases, or situation reports for norovirus in the United States during the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, New York DOH, Texas DSHS) often publish outbreak-specific reports with subnational location, case counts, and dates that supplement national surveillance.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR) articles or notices reporting norovirus outbreaks or case counts in the United States for the target period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR frequently publishes norovirus outbreak investigations with confirmed case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and evidence quotes suitable for extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO or PAHO situation reports or disease outbreak news referencing norovirus activity in the United States during 2024-12-01 to 2025-02-28.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports provide independent aggregate summaries that can validate CDC-reported figures without being the primary collection source.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured databases such as HealthMap, ProMED, or GOARN alerts referencing norovirus outbreaks in the United States during the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured alert databases aggregate outbreak signals from multiple sources and can serve as independent validation of case counts and outbreak events.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definition pages, norovirus background pages, and surveillance methodology documents to support correct interpretation of case classification fields.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC's case definitions for confirmed, probable, and suspected norovirus is essential for correctly populating cases_confirmed, cases_probable, and cases_suspected fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature published in 2024-2025 describing norovirus epidemiology, outbreak patterns, or surveillance methodology in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Recent literature provides context for interpreting surveillance data, genotype distributions, and outbreak settings relevant to the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news reports covering specific norovirus outbreaks in the United States from December 2024 through February 2025, particularly those citing official case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may surface outbreak events (e.g., cruise ship, school, long-term care facility) with case counts and dates before official reports are published, serving as leads for official source follow-up.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (e.g., cumulative vs. newly reported, suspected vs. confirmed), where validation and collection roles may overlap, or where subnational attribution is unclear.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Norovirus surveillance data often mixes outbreak-level and aggregate counts; human review is needed to resolve ambiguous count types and prevent validation leakage.

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC NoroSTAT norovirus surveillance 2024 2025 season United States cases outbreaks
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: CDC NoroSTAT is the primary US national norovirus surveillance system. This query directly targets the CDC's seasonal surveillance summary, which is the highest-priority authoritative source for national-level case and outbreak counts. Natural-language phrasing without exact-phrase quoting improves recall over the upstream query formulation.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC NoroSTAT weekly surveillance summary or season overview page with outbreak counts, case totals, and trend data for the 2024-2025 norovirus season
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; authored by CDC Division of Viral Diseases; references NORS data

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC NORS norovirus outbreak reports United States December 2024 January February 2025 cases hospitalizations deaths
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) is the CDC's structured database for foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks including norovirus. It provides outbreak-level records with subnational location, setting, case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths — directly mapping to the target fields. Querying NORS for the specific months in the task window maximizes coverage of the locality and subnational_location fields.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC NORS dashboard or data summary page listing individual norovirus outbreak records with setting, state, case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths for the target date range
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov/nors domain; structured outbreak-level records with state and setting fields

iterative_search_queries.query: norovirus outbreak United States winter 2024 2025 cases deaths state health department report
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Because norovirus is not nationally notifiable, subnational outbreak data is primarily reported at the state and local level. This broad web search targets state health department reports and press releases that would populate the subnational_location and locality fields. The query avoids exact-phrase quoting to maximize recall across diverse state agency naming conventions.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: State or local health department press releases, epidemiology bulletins, or outbreak investigation reports with specific case counts, dates, and geographic locations within the US
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: State .gov domains (e.g., health.state.xx.us); official press release or epi bulletin format; named public health official quoted

iterative_search_queries.query: norovirus surge outbreak United States 2025 cases hospitalizations news January February
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: News sources provide timely coverage of norovirus outbreaks that may precede official surveillance summaries, and often cite official figures that can be traced back to primary sources. The term 'surge' is included because media coverage of norovirus in winter 2024-2025 is likely to use this framing. This query covers the later portion of the time window (Jan-Feb 2025) where news coverage is most likely to be available.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: News articles from credible outlets (AP, Reuters, major US newspapers, health news sites) reporting on norovirus case surges, specific outbreak events, or official statistics for the US in the target window, ideally citing CDC or state health department figures
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: Bylined article from established news organization; quotes from CDC spokesperson or state health official; references specific case counts or outbreak numbers

iterative_search_queries.query: norovirus outbreaks United States February 2025 cases weekly CDC data

This query targets news coverage of norovirus activity in February 2025, which is likely to cite CDC weekly NoroSTAT figures for that period. News sources are the fastest path to February 2025 data given the lag in official surveillance summaries.

iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: Bylined article from established news outlet (AP, Reuters, NBC, CBS, CNN, CIDRAP) published in February 2025; cites CDC spokesperson or official weekly count

collection_spec.data_focus: human Norovirus case, outbreak, and surveillance data
collection_spec.user_request: Collect Norovirus cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for United States from 2024-12-01 to 2025-02-28.

official_source_terms: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention norovirus
likely_reporting_agencies: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists (CSTE)
European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) — for comparative context
disease_intelligence.suggested_geographic_granularity: ["national (United States)", "state", "county", "city/locality", "institutional setting (e.g., school, long-term care facility, cruise ship, restaurant)"]
disease_intelligence.suggested_time_granularity: ["weekly (preferred for surveillance data)", "monthly (for aggregate reports)", "outbreak-specific date range (onset to resolution)", "date of report publication"]
count_semantics_notes: Norovirus case counts are frequently reported as 'ill persons' or 'affected individuals' rather than confirmed/probable/suspected — map to cases_unspecified unless laboratory confirmation is explicitly stated.
Laboratory-confirmed cases (RT-PCR or EIA) should be mapped to cases_confirmed.
Outbreak-level counts may aggregate across multiple case classification tiers — note aggregation in evidence_quote.
Attack rates are commonly reported for institutional outbreaks; derive absolute case counts only if denominator (population at risk) is explicitly stated.
Death counts for norovirus are rare and often reported only in vulnerable populations (elderly, immunocompromised); treat with high specificity — do not infer deaths from severity language alone.
Hospitalization counts may be reported separately from case counts; extract independently and note if derived from outbreak investigation vs. surveillance aggregate.
Seasonal surveillance data (e.g., NoroSTAT) reports activity levels (low/moderate/high/very high) rather than absolute case counts — do not convert activity levels to numeric case counts.
NORS data may report both primary and secondary cases; note distinction in evidence_quote.
Some state reports aggregate norovirus with 'acute gastroenteritis' — only extract if norovirus is explicitly named or laboratory-confirmed.
disambiguation_risks: 'Stomach flu' and 'stomach bug' are colloquial terms that may refer to norovirus or other enteric pathogens — require laboratory confirmation or explicit norovirus attribution before extraction.
Rotavirus, adenovirus, and sapovirus outbreaks may be reported alongside norovirus — extract only norovirus-specific counts.
Calicivirus may refer to animal calicivirus (e.g., feline calicivirus) — confirm human norovirus context.
'Viral gastroenteritis' without pathogen specification should be mapped to cases_unspecified and flagged for validation.
Norwalk virus is an older synonym — treat as norovirus if context confirms human enteric illness.
Norovirus GII.4 Sydney variant surges may be reported separately from aggregate norovirus counts — note genotype in evidence_quote if available.
Foodborne illness outbreak reports may list multiple pathogens; extract only norovirus-attributed counts.
Winter vomiting disease is a UK-centric term but may appear in US media coverage — confirm norovirus etiology before extraction.
exclusion_terms: norovirus environmental sampling only (no human cases)
suggested_query_templates: norovirus gastroenteritis outbreak United States December 2024
warnings: task_input_warnings carried forward: source_discovery_not_yet_disease_generic — source discovery logic must be validated for norovirus-specific source types before deployment.
task_input_warnings carried forward: extraction_record_model_still_hantavirus_named — confirm extraction record schema has been updated to norovirus before data entry.

Norovirus is NOT a nationally notifiable disease in the United States at the federal level; case counts are primarily captured through outbreak investigations (NORS) and sentinel surveillance (NoroSTAT/CaliciNet), not mandatory individual case reporting — aggregate and outbreak-level data will dominate.
NoroSTAT reports activity levels (not absolute case counts) — do not attempt numeric extraction from activity-level fields.
Seasonal peak for norovirus in the US is November–April; the target window (Dec 2024–Feb 2025) falls within peak season — expect elevated outbreak report volume.
Cruise ship outbreaks are reported to CDC Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) separately from land-based outbreaks — include VSP as a distinct source category.

The CaliciNet data snippet references 'September 1, 2024 – August 31, 2025 (n=411)' confirmed outbreaks — this covers the full task window but the breakdown by month or week is not visible in the snippet and cannot be assumed.

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC NoroSTAT norovirus surveillance 2024 2025 season United States cases outbreaks
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: CDC NoroSTAT is the primary US national norovirus surveillance system. This query directly targets the CDC's seasonal surveillance summary, which is the highest-priority authoritative source for national-level case and outbreak counts. Natural-language phrasing without exact-phrase quoting improves recall over the upstream query formulation.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC NoroSTAT weekly surveillance summary or season overview page with outbreak counts, case totals, and trend data for the 2024-2025 norovirus season
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; authored by CDC Division of Viral Diseases; references NORS data

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC NORS norovirus outbreak reports United States December 2024 January February 2025 cases hospitalizations deaths
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) is the CDC's structured database for foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks including norovirus. It provides outbreak-level records with subnational location, setting, case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths — directly mapping to the target fields. Querying NORS for the specific months in the task window maximizes coverage of the locality and subnational_location fields.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC NORS dashboard or data summary page listing individual norovirus outbreak records with setting, state, case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths for the target date range
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov/nors domain; structured outbreak-level records with state and setting fields

iterative_search_queries.query: norovirus outbreak United States winter 2024 2025 cases deaths state health department report
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Because norovirus is not nationally notifiable, subnational outbreak data is primarily reported at the state and local level. This broad web search targets state health department reports and press releases that would populate the subnational_location and locality fields. The query avoids exact-phrase quoting to maximize recall across diverse state agency naming conventions.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: State or local health department press releases, epidemiology bulletins, or outbreak investigation reports with specific case counts, dates, and geographic locations within the US
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: State .gov domains (e.g., health.state.xx.us); official press release or epi bulletin format; named public health official quoted

iterative_search_queries.query: norovirus surge outbreak United States 2025 cases hospitalizations news January February
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: News sources provide timely coverage of norovirus outbreaks that may precede official surveillance summaries, and often cite official figures that can be traced back to primary sources. The term 'surge' is included because media coverage of norovirus in winter 2024-2025 is likely to use this framing. This query covers the later portion of the time window (Jan-Feb 2025) where news coverage is most likely to be available.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: News articles from credible outlets (AP, Reuters, major US newspapers, health news sites) reporting on norovirus case surges, specific outbreak events, or official statistics for the US in the target window, ideally citing CDC or state health department figures
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: Bylined article from established news organization; quotes from CDC spokesperson or state health official; references specific case counts or outbreak numbers

iterative_search_queries.query: norovirus outbreaks United States February 2025 cases weekly CDC data
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: The February 2025 portion of the task window (Feb 1–28) is entirely uncovered by iteration 1 results. This query targets news coverage of norovirus activity in February 2025, which is likely to cite CDC weekly NoroSTAT figures for that period. News sources are the fastest path to February 2025 data given the lag in official surveillance summaries.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: News articles from February 2025 reporting on norovirus outbreak counts, trends, or specific events in the US, citing CDC or state health department data for that month
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: Bylined article from established news outlet (AP, Reuters, NBC, CBS, CNN, CIDRAP) published in February 2025; cites CDC spokesperson or official weekly count
iterative_search_queries.previous_iteration_basis: iter1_q4 — iteration 1 news query covered Jan 2025 well but February 2025 data is absent from all returned snippets

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC NORS National Outbreak Reporting System norovirus 2024 2025 outbreak data hospitalizations deaths setting
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: The CDC NORS dashboard is the primary structured source for outbreak-level records including setting (e.g., restaurant, school, long-term care), state, case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths. Despite being queried in iteration 1, no direct NORS dashboard result was returned. This query reformulates the search to target the NORS dashboard or summary page more directly, which is critical for populating the deaths, hospitalizations, subnational_location, and locality fields.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC NORS dashboard page or annual/quarterly summary with tabular outbreak records for norovirus in 2024-2025, including columns for state, setting, cases, hospitalizations, deaths
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov/nors domain; structured table with outbreak-level records; CDC Division of Foodborne, Waterborne, and Environmental Diseases authorship
iterative_search_queries.previous_iteration_basis: iter1_q2 — NORS database query did not return a direct NORS dashboard result; reformulated to improve targeting

iterative_search_queries.query: norovirus outbreak 2025 state health department cases report school nursing home restaurant
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Iteration 1 returned only one state health department result (Minnesota). Subnational and locality coverage is a key gap. This query broadens the search to capture state-level outbreak investigation reports across multiple settings (schools, nursing homes, restaurants) — the most common norovirus outbreak settings — which would populate the subnational_location, locality, and setting-specific case count fields. Including setting terms improves recall for state epi bulletins and press releases.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: State or county health department press releases, epidemiology bulletins, or outbreak investigation reports from December 2024–February 2025 with specific case counts, dates, and named locations within US states
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: State .gov domains (e.g., health.state.xx.us, doh.xx.gov); official press release or epi bulletin format; named epidemiologist or public health official quoted; specific case counts and dates
iterative_search_queries.previous_iteration_basis: iter1_q3 — only one state health department result (Minnesota) returned; this query adds setting terms to improve subnational recall

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC norovirus cruise ship vessel outbreak December 2024 January February 2025 cases
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: The CIDRAP snippet from iteration 1 mentioned '16 cruise ship norovirus outbreaks reported in 2024, including 5 in December.' CDC's Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) tracks cruise ship outbreaks separately from NoroSTAT/NORS and publishes outbreak investigation reports with specific case counts, ship names, and dates — directly populating the locality and cases_unspecified fields. This is a distinct and well-documented data channel for norovirus that was not covered in iteration 1.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) outbreak investigation reports or summary page listing cruise ship norovirus outbreaks in December 2024–February 2025 with ship name, case counts, and dates; or CIDRAP/news follow-up citing VSP data
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov/nceh/vsp domain; VSP outbreak investigation report format with ship name, voyage dates, case counts; or CIDRAP article citing VSP data
